message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (dir. Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1968 | **Night of the Living Dead** (dir. George A. Romero) | The original zombie film that defined a genre. |
| 1974 | **The Texas Chain Saw Massacre** (dir. Tobe Hooper) | Raw, gritty horror that still feels visceral. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (dir. Stanley Kubrick) | A chilling psychological thriller with iconic imagery. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (dir. Wes Craven) | Introduced Freddy Krueger and redefined slasher films. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (dir. Jonathan Demme) | A tense psychological thriller with unforgettable characters. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (dir. Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered the found‑footage style and created a cultural phenomenon. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (dir. Danny Boyle) | Revitalized the zombie genre with high‑speed dread. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (dir. James Wan) | A new kind of horror that combined gore with moral dilemmas. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (dir. Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage film that made a huge impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (dir. James Wan) | A modern supernatural thriller that sparked a franchise. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (dir. Drew Goddard) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (dir. David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (dir. Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burning, atmospheric horror set in Puritan New England. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that blends satire and terror. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (dir. John Krasinski) | A tense thriller where silence is survival. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (dir. Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that’s as unsettling as it is beautiful. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (dir. Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of a classic story with a strong female lead. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (dir. Nia DaCosta) | A fresh take on a horror legend with a powerful social message. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (dir. Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller that blends creepy atmosphere with a gripping plot. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (dir. Gerard Johnstone) | A horror‑comedy about a killer doll that’s both funny and frightening. |

Feel free to pick any era or sub‑genre that intrigues you—whether you’re into psychological dread, supernatural chills, or slasher thrills. Enjoy the scares!
